cells.tense: Right now, the build is holding steady, and the hands are steady with it.
cells.act: hold space for what someone feels without fixing it
cells.ask: Someone near you is carrying something heavy this week. Stay with what they feel instead of handing them a solution. Let the answer wait.
cells.core:
You can carry weight without gripping it. A project, a room, a thing you're making — it holds because you built it to, not because you're bearing down on it right now. And when someone near you is carrying something, you can stand beside them without reaching in to solve it. That's the balance: the strength is the builder's, and the space around it is real.

The place to aim next is other people's feeling. You're good at holding the structure; the living piece is staying with a feeling without making it a job. When it's heavy, don't shape it. Stay near it. What you've built in yourself is steady enough to stand next to something unshaped and not reach for the tools.
cells.sheetLine: You build so it holds, and you can let it hold.
cells.verb: building what holds — raising the structure that will stand after the hands that made it are done
cells.place: where grip gets opened on purpose — the deliberate clearing of space for what comes next

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead of you, a future is being braced against before it can be built.
cells.act: make the fair call about a feeling, yourself
cells.ask: When a feeling runs hot this week — yours or someone's near you — hold the ruling until it finishes moving. Make the call then, at the size the feeling actually is.
cells.core:
The build is running ahead of itself. You're pouring foundations for a house whose plans changed last week, tightening what isn't ready to be held. The strength is real; the timing is not. When a thing is pushed into its final shape before it has settled, the shape breaks later, and the rebuilding lands on somebody — often on you.

What's left to do is smaller than what you've been doing. You don't need to manage the feeling before it lands. Let one run its course without a verdict on it, then rule once the air is clear. That's the fair call, made by you, at the pace feeling actually moves.

cells.tense: Something finished, and the hands are still on the old tools.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what is not
cells.ask: There's something that finished a while back and is still being held open. Write a page on what it gave you, close the page, and add nothing more to it.
cells.core:
The build here has stalled, and it isn't the work that stopped — the closing didn't happen. What's done is being held as if the outcome could still change. The hands are still on it, and the tools are still out. The strength to release is the same strength that built the thing in the first place; it just hasn't been called on.

One completion, acknowledged right, returns the current. So finish something on purpose — not the project, the putting down of it. What it gave you is already in your hands. Set down what's left over, and the next thing to build gets a builder with free hands.
cells.sheetLine: The build is done and you're still holding the tools.

cells.tense: The structure stands, and the record of who raised it has gone quiet.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Begin something with no plan, no use, and nobody to show it to. Start it and stop it before it turns into a project.
cells.core:
What you keep standing, keeps standing — quietly, without a marker that says who made it. You do that so well the structure looks like it was there before anyone touched it. And the piece that's missing is the plain delight of the start: the unbuilt pleasure of beginning something just because it began.

The correction is smaller than the pattern. Go back toward the first move — the one before it has a use. Whatever you start doesn't need to become anything. It only needs to be yours at the start, where the spark lives. That's the part that got folded away for the structure to hold.
